kind: v29 gap scale derived + 97-bit transfer arm + per-walk kappa + ledger

construction.design: production walks nb = 2^66 A-pool bases per side, ell = ceil(N/nb) steps each

gap_law.kind: DERIVED gap scale (v29 fix of the 2^12 mis-charge)
gap_law.derivation: mu(q) = d*ln q with d = 2^20 and walk band q_w ~ 2^76 gives mu = 2^(20 + log2(52.68)) = 2^25.719 = 5.524e+07; the list holds ell = 883576288830423 = 2^49.65 gaps, so the realised maximum is mu*(ln ell + gamma) = 2^30.848, i.e. the even-gap support must run to < 2^31. v28 charged 2^11 (the HOME_BITS=12 recovery STEP COUNT in keymod.py, a different object) as if it were the gap MAGNITUDE: wrong by 2^19.0.
gap_law.table_construction: T_i[2j] = [2j*a_i]P0 for even gaps 2,4,...,<2^31 is built by the even-gap ADDITION CHAIN T_i[2]=2*(a_iP0), T_i[2j]=T_i[2(j-1)]+T_i[2]: one group addition per entry, charged at 15 ops/entry (12 doublings + 3 additions) as a stress rule
gap_law.per_base_cost: GAP_SUPPORT = 2^30 additions per base vs ell = 2^49.65 steps, i.e. 2^-19.65 of the walk

tail.note: a gap above the support is priced per base as a 32-doubling small-scalar multiple of a_iP0 (62 group ops); ONE worst-case occurrence is charged as a bound, which covers the measured-law expectation 0.01154

pool_scalar.what_it_is: the pool entry is a 97-bit INTEGER EXPONENT a_i (keymod.py: 'stored 97-bit pool entry'; 2 LDP per candidate). The record scalar is a_i*w_k: 97-bit base x 77-bit walk element = a 174-bit product, and 174 < log2(m) = 234.857, so the product NEVER wraps mod m: production ratios are ratios of exact integers, not residues of a uniform draw.
pool_scalar.why_it_matters: a_i uniform in H (the v28 arm) and a_i uniform in [1,2^97) are different base laws: H has order m = 2^234.857, so 2^97 covers only 2^-137.9 of it. The hit test only sees the RATIO SET {a_i w_k/(u b_j w_l)}, whose size is 6N^2 = 2^233.89 either way (N^2 base-ratios x walk-ratios, 6 from mu6), compared against |H| = 2^234.857; so the pair law 1-exp(-K), K = 6N^2/m, is a statement about the ratio map, not about the base support.

arm.design: SAME walk object and SAME density as the primary arm (nb=22, ell=6944, K=0.509420), but bases drawn from an INTERVAL [1,2^18) instead of uniform in H, and with span+walk_band = 39 < 41 so the products a_i*w_k are EXACT (no mod-p wrap): the production pool-scalar regime at reduced absolute scale.

control_same_geometry_uniform_bases.note: identical nb/ell/K/seed family with full-support bases: the base-law change is the only difference between this row and the pool arm

pool_scalar.confound_disclosed: an earlier run of this arm drew BOTH the bases and the target v from [1,2^18). That moves the TARGET law (production v is uniform in H) and collapsed q to 0.0627 for that reason, not for a pool reason; the harness now pins v to uniform-in-H and the arm was re-run. The discarded run is recorded here rather than deleted, because the confound was ours.

kappa.method: PER-WALK measurement: each walk (one trial = one full record set at the primary rung) contributes kappa_walk = (collisions in that walk)/(uniform expectation C(N,2)/m); mean/p50/p95/p99/MAX are over WALKS. v28 used 12 big + 4 small census AGGREGATES from kappa-v26 as if they were 16 walks.
kappa.granularity: the per-walk collision count is integer-valued with expectation 0.0425, so one extra duplicate moves kappa_walk by 23.56: the MAX is a conservative charge by construction
kappa.transfer: K = 6N^2/m is held at the production value, and the per-walk duplicate expectation depends only on K, so the measured per-walk tail is scale-free between fixture and production
